---
title: "Pre-Bootstrap Checklist"
---

Before bootstrapping real existing repositories, use this sequence.

## 1. Advise

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo
```

Use the recommendation to choose a starting stage and profile set. Default to `research-heavy` when terminology, docs, or project intent are thin.

## 2. Audit

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo
```

Inspect conflicts before writing anything. If the repository already has important docs or agent files, prefer targeted add commands over full bootstrap.

## 3. Start With Memory And Core Skills

For most existing repositories, first add memory guidance, knowledge lookup, scope-drift control, plan review, and API docs lookup:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill cq --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill session-focus --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill grill-with-docs --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill get-api-docs --apply
```

## 4. Add Docs Or Models Next

Add docs if the project lacks durable project memory:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-docs --path /path/to/repo --apply
```

Add model profiles if agents need explicit model/provider defaults:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-model --path /path/to/repo --model-profile default-coding --apply
```

## 5. Add Safety And Parallelism When Needed

For prompt DAGs, model migration, or prompt-heavy repos, add prompt and repo-map guidance before rewriting prompts:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-prompts --path /path/to/repo --prompt-profile prompt-migration-gpt55 --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-prompts --path /path/to/repo --prompt-profile prompt-evals-dag --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-repomap --path /path/to/repo --repomap-profile hamilton-dag --apply
```

For user-facing AI, policy, education, children, or privacy-sensitive repos, add safety and privacy guidance:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-safety --path /path/to/repo --safety-profile prompt-output-safety --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-privacy --path /path/to/repo --privacy-profile data-privacy-review --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-public-interest --path /path/to/repo --public-interest-profile child-rights-digital --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill security-audit --apply
```

Use sandboxing before running unknown scripts, generated code, package installs, or risky test suites:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-sandbox --path /path/to/repo --sandbox-profile sandbox-light --apply
```

Use worktree guidance for parallel prototypes or multiple agents:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-worktree --path /path/to/repo --worktree-profile parallel-worktrees --apply
```

## 6. Check Drift

After bootstrap, use:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /path/to/repo
```

Use `check` before later upgrades or stage transitions.

## 7. Classify Upstream Candidates

After local changes to generated assets, use:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo
```

Pair this with the `upstream-improvement` skill before copying any downstream change back into the Reference Source.

## 8. Preview Upgrade Readiness

Before any future write-capable upgrade, use the read-only preview:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo
```

The current command does not write files. It reports user-review items, blockers, and unavailable update candidates.
